The desk's screener calls it gapping when the open is 3% or more above (or below) the prior close. Gaps come from news that arrived while the market was shut: earnings, guidance, a deal, an upgrade. The gap itself is not the trade; what the stock does with the gap is. A gap up on earnings that holds its opening range and keeps going on heavy volume is a Power Earnings Gap; a gap up that fades back into the prior day's range is a failure. Gap support, where the bottom of the gap holds on the next pullback, is one of the desk's levels.

after: The stock is trading within 5% of its highest price of the past year. A stock near its highs has little overhead supply: most people who bought it in the past year are in profit, so there are few trapped holders waiting to sell into strength. At new highs means it printed a fresh 52-week high today. The desk buys strength, so near the highs is where it shops, in a market that allows it. The opposite, a stock far below its highs, carries overhead supply at every level it fell through. The 52-week high is the standard lookback; a stock near all-time highs is the same idea with no supply at all above it.
